nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a TRIP-Stern tree with left transition $L$. For every natural number $n$, the left-most node of $T$ at depth $n + 1$ equals $L$ applied to the left-most node of $T$ at depth $n$.
nodes.title: Recursion for the left-most node

nodes.summary: For every TRIP-Stern tree $T$, the left-most node of $T$ at depth $0$ is the seed of $T$.
nodes.title: Left-most node at depth zero

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a TRIP-Stern tree with seed $s$ and left transition $L$. The left-most node of $T$ at depth $n$ is $L^n(s)$, the result of applying $L$ $n$ times to $s$; that is, it is $s$ at depth $0$, and at depth $n + 1$ it is $L$ applied to the left-most node at depth $n$.
nodes.title: Left-most node of a TRIP-Stern tree

nodes.summary: For every TRIP-Stern tree $T$, the node of $T$ selected by the empty binary path is the seed of $T$.
nodes.title: The empty path selects the seed

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a TRIP-Stern tree with left transition $L$. For every binary path $p$, the node of $T$ selected by $p$ followed by one left step equals $L$ applied to the node of $T$ selected by $p$.
nodes.title: Extending a path by a left step

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a TRIP-Stern tree with right transition $R$. For every binary path $p$, the node of $T$ selected by $p$ followed by one right step equals $R$ applied to the node of $T$ selected by $p$.
nodes.title: Extending a path by a right step

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a TRIP-Stern tree with seed $s$, left transition $L$ and right transition $R$. A binary path is a finite sequence of steps, each left or right. The node of $T$ selected by a path $(b_1, \dots, b_k)$ is obtained by starting at $s$ and applying, for $i = 1, \dots, k$ in order, $L$ if $b_i$ is a left step and $R$ if $b_i$ is a right step.
nodes.title: Node selected by a binary path

nodes.summary: For every TRIP-Stern tree $T$, natural number $n$ and node value $y$, $y$ lies in the set of nodes of $T$ at depth $n$ if and only if there is a binary path of length $n$ whose selected node in $T$ is $y$.
nodes.title: Membership in a level of a TRIP-Stern tree

nodes.summary: For every TRIP-Stern tree $T$ and every node value $y$, $y$ lies in the set of nodes of $T$ at depth $0$ if and only if $y$ is the seed of $T$.
nodes.title: Depth zero is the seed

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a TRIP-Stern tree and $n$ a natural number. The set of nodes of $T$ at depth $n$ is the set of all values $y$ such that some binary path of length $n$ selects $y$ in $T$.
nodes.title: Nodes at a given depth of a TRIP-Stern tree

nodes.summary: For every TRIP-Stern tree $T$ and every natural number $n$, the rightmost node of $T$ at depth $n + 1$ is the image of the rightmost node of $T$ at depth $n$ under the right transition of $T$.
nodes.title: Successor step of the rightmost node

nodes.summary: For every TRIP-Stern tree $T$, the rightmost node of $T$ at depth $0$ is the seed of $T$.
nodes.title: Rightmost node at depth zero

nodes.summary: For a TRIP-Stern tree $T$ and a natural number $n$, the rightmost node of $T$ at depth $n$ is obtained from the seed of $T$ by applying the right transition of $T$ exactly $n$ times: at depth $0$ it is the seed, and at depth $n + 1$ it is the image of the rightmost node at depth $n$ under the right transition.
nodes.title: Rightmost node of a TRIP-Stern tree

nodes.summary: A TRIP-Stern tree with node values in a type $\alpha$ consists of a root seed in $\alpha$ together with two maps from $\alpha$ to $\alpha$, the left transition and the right transition. No condition is imposed on the seed or on the two transitions; in the source the seed is $(1,1,1)$ and the left and right transitions are induced by the maps $F_0$ and $F_1$ defined there.
nodes.title: TRIP-Stern tree

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
